faqs.question: How do I calculate percentage?
faqs.answer: Divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100. Example: 25/50 × 100 = 50%.

faqs.question: What is X% of Y?
faqs.answer: Multiply Y by X and divide by 100. Example: 15% of 200 = (15 × 200) / 100 = 30.

faqs.question: How do I calculate percentage increase?
How do I reverse a percentage?
faqs.answer: To find original before X% increase: Current ÷ (1 + X/100).

faqs.question: What's percentage points vs percentage?
faqs.answer: 5% to 8% = 3 percentage points increase, but 60% relative increase.

faqs.question: How do I add fractions?
faqs.answer: Find common denominator, add numerators, keep denominator, simplify. 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

faqs.question: How do I multiply fractions?
faqs.answer: Multiply numerators, multiply denominators. 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.

faqs.question: How do I divide fractions?
faqs.answer: Flip the second fraction and multiply. 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2.

faqs.question: What's a mixed number?
faqs.answer: A whole number plus a fraction, like 2½. Convert: 2½ = 5/2.

faqs.question: How do I simplify fractions?
faqs.answer: Divide numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor. 6/8 = 3/4.

faqs.answer: b² - 4ac. Positive = 2 real solutions. Zero = 1 solution. Negative = complex solutions.

education/college-gpa.metaDescription: Free college GPA calculator for semester and cumulative GPA. Track your university grades and plan what you need to graduate.
education/college-gpa.introText: Track your college GPA by semester and cumulatively. Enter credit hours and grades to see where you stand and what you need to reach your goals.
education/college-gpa.formula: GPA = Σ(Grade Points × Credit Hours) / Σ Credit Hours

benefits.title: Goal Planner
benefits.description: What grades to reach target GPA

faqs.question: How is college GPA calculated?
faqs.answer: Multiply each grade's points by credit hours, sum all, divide by total credit hours.

faqs.question: Is college GPA on a 4.0 scale?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. A=4.0, B=3.0, C=2.0, D=1.0, F=0. Some use A+=4.33.

faqs.question: How do I calculate cumulative GPA?
faqs.answer: Include all semesters. Total grade points ÷ total credit hours.

faqs.question: What GPA do I need for grad school?
faqs.answer: Generally 3.0+ minimum, 3.5+ for competitive programs.

faqs.question: Can I improve a low GPA?
faqs.answer: Yes, but it takes time. Use our goal calculator to plan needed grades.

education/test-score.name: Test Score
education/test-score.metaTitle: Test Score Calculator - Points to Percentage | CalcMaster
education/test-score.metaDescription: Free test score calculator converts points to percentage and letter grade. See what you scored and what it means.
education/test-score.introText: Got your test back? Enter points earned and total points to see your percentage and letter grade instantly.

benefits.title: Letter Grade
benefits.description: See your A, B, C, D, or F

faqs.question: How do I calculate my test score?
faqs.answer: Points earned ÷ total points × 100. Got 42 out of 50? That's 84%.

faqs.question: What letter grade is 85%?
faqs.answer: On standard scale, 85% is a B. Ranges vary by school.

faqs.question: How do I find total points if I only know percentage?
faqs.answer: If you know points earned and percentage, divide points by percentage.

faqs.question: What if my teacher uses a curve?
faqs.answer: Enter curved score, or calculate raw score first then apply curve.

faqs.question: How do I calculate weighted test score?
faqs.answer: Multiply score by test weight, then add to other weighted components.

education/study-timer.introText: Boost your study efficiency with our Pomodoro-style timer. Set focused study sessions with breaks to maximize retention and avoid burnout.
education/study-timer.formula: Pomodoro: 25 min study + 5 min break × 4, then 15-30 min long break

faqs.question: What is the Pomodoro technique?
faqs.answer: Study for 25 minutes, take 5 minute break. After 4 cycles, take a longer 15-30 minute break.

faqs.question: Why are timed sessions effective?
faqs.answer: Short focused bursts prevent fatigue and improve concentration. Breaks help consolidate learning.

faqs.question: How many Pomodoros should I do?
faqs.answer: Depends on your schedule. 4-8 pomodoros (2-4 hours) is a productive day for most.

faqs.question: Can I customize the times?
faqs.answer: Yes, set any work/break intervals that suit your focus style.

faqs.question: Does this track total study time?
faqs.answer: Yes, we log completed sessions so you can see daily and weekly totals.

date-time/timezone.introText: Convert time between any time zones instantly. Perfect for scheduling international meetings, calls, or planning travel.
date-time/timezone.formula: Local Time = UTC ± Time Zone Offset

faqs.question: How do I convert time zones?
faqs.answer: Select source city/zone, enter time, select destination zone. We show converted time.

faqs.question: What is UTC?
faqs.answer: Coordinated Universal Time - the reference time zone (GMT+0). All zones are offsets from UTC.

faqs.question: Does it handle daylight saving?
faqs.answer: Yes, we automatically account for DST in all locations that observe it.

faqs.question: How do I find meeting time for multiple people?
faqs.answer: Add multiple time zones to see overlapping business hours.

faqs.question: What time zone am I in?
faqs.answer: We detect your local time zone automatically. You can also search by city.

date-time/timecard.formula: Total Hours = Σ(Clock Out - Clock In - Breaks) per day

faqs.question: How do I fill out a time card?
faqs.answer: Enter start time, end time, and break time for each day worked.

faqs.question: How is overtime calculated?
faqs.answer: Hours over 8/day or 40/week are overtime. We show regular and OT hours separately.

faqs.question: Can I calculate bi-weekly hours?
faqs.answer: Yes, fill in two weeks of data for bi-weekly pay periods.

faqs.question: How do I convert time to decimal?
faqs.answer: We show hours in both HH:MM and decimal format. 7:30 = 7.5 hours.

faqs.question: Can I print my timecard?
faqs.answer: Yes, print or export your completed timecard.

construction/tile.name: Tile
secondaryKeywords: how many tiles do i need
construction/tile.metaTitle: Tile Calculator - How Many Tiles Do I Need? | CalcMaster
construction/tile.metaDescription: Free tile calculator estimates tiles needed for floors, walls, and backsplashes. Account for waste and see cost estimates.
construction/tile.heroSubtitle: Calculate how many tiles you need
construction/tile.introText: Planning a tile project? Our calculator estimates the number of tiles needed for floors, walls, showers, or backsplashes with waste factor included.

benefits.title: Cost Estimate
benefits.description: Enter price per tile or sqft

faqs.question: How do I calculate tiles needed?
faqs.answer: Measure area in sqft, divide by tile area in sqft, add 10-15% for waste.

faqs.question: How much extra tile should I buy?
faqs.answer: 10% for simple layouts, 15% for diagonal or complex patterns, 20% for large format.

faqs.question: How do I calculate tile for a wall?
faqs.answer: Height × Width for each wall. Subtract windows and doors.

faqs.question: What size tile is best?
faqs.answer: Depends on room size. Large tiles make small rooms look bigger but need more cuts.

faqs.question: How do I account for grout lines?
faqs.answer: Our calculator includes standard grout spacing. Adjust for thick grout lines.

construction/paint.name: Paint
secondaryKeywords: how much paint do i need
construction/paint.metaTitle: Paint Calculator - How Much Paint Do I Need? | CalcMaster
construction/paint.metaDescription: Free paint calculator estimates gallons needed for any room. Factor in doors, windows, and number of coats for accurate coverage.
construction/paint.heroSubtitle: Calculate how much paint you need
construction/paint.introText: Painting a room? Our calculator estimates gallons of paint needed based on wall area, coats, and paint coverage rate.

faqs.question: How much paint do I need?
faqs.answer: One gallon covers about 350-400 sqft per coat. Measure walls and divide.

faqs.question: How many coats of paint?
faqs.answer: Usually 2 coats. 1 coat if same color, 3 if covering dark with light.

faqs.question: Should I subtract doors and windows?
faqs.answer: Yes, we automatically deduct standard sizes. Enter actual sizes for accuracy.

faqs.question: How do I calculate for textured walls?
faqs.answer: Reduce coverage by 20-25% for textured surfaces.

faqs.question: How much primer do I need?
faqs.answer: Same calculation as paint. One coat primer for new drywall or major color change.

construction/btu.name: BTU
construction/btu.metaTitle: BTU Calculator - AC & Heating Size for Room | CalcMaster
construction/btu.metaDescription: Free BTU calculator sizes air conditioners and heaters for any room. Enter dimensions and get the right BTU rating for comfort.
construction/btu.heroSubtitle: Size your AC or heater correctly
construction/btu.introText: Get the right size AC or heater for your room. Our BTU calculator considers room size, ceiling height, insulation, and climate for accurate sizing.
construction/btu.formula: Base BTU = Room Sqft × 20, adjusted for factors

faqs.question: What is BTU?
faqs.answer: British Thermal Unit - measures heating/cooling capacity. Higher BTU = more powerful.

faqs.question: How many BTUs per square foot?
faqs.answer: General rule: 20 BTU per sqft for AC. Varies by climate and room factors.

faqs.question: What happens if AC is too small?
faqs.answer: Won't cool adequately, runs constantly, higher energy bills, reduced lifespan.

faqs.question: What if AC is too big?
faqs.answer: Short cycles, poor humidity control, uneven cooling, wasted energy.

faqs.question: How do windows affect BTU?
faqs.answer: More/larger windows increase BTU needs by 10-20%. South-facing adds more.
